chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man is confined (by illness), he should send forward his sacrificial animal. So when he recovers and finds lightness in himself, let him proceed if he thinks he can catch up with the people. So if he arrives in Makkah before slaughtering the sacrificial animal, let him remain in his Ihram until he completes all the rituals, and let him slaughter his animal, and there is nothing upon him. And if he arrives in Makkah and his animal has already been slaughtered, then upon him is the Hajj next year or the Umrah.

I said, 'And if he dies while in Ihram before he reaches Makkah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Hajj should be performed on his behalf if it was the Hajj of Islam, and Umrah should be performed on his behalf; it is merely a debt upon him.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.إِحْصَار: Confinement or prevention from completing Hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for a pilgrim who falls ill or is confined during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the fiqh of *Hadi* (sacrificial animal) for the *Muhsar* (one prevented from completing Hajj), emphasizing the distinction between the obligatory Hajj and voluntary acts. It clarifies that if one dies in Ihram before reaching Makkah, their heirs perform Hajj on their behalf if it was their first obligatory Hajj, reflecting the Shia view of *Hajj al-Ni'ab* (substitute pilgrimage). The ruling underscores the continuity of ritual state (*Ihram*) until the completion of all rites, ensuring the pilgrim's obligation is fully discharged.
